messages.subject: NimbleSCR Prior Predictive Checks/Discrepancy
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to follow best practices for integrated population models, but I'm not sure how to implement prior predictive checks or discrepancy measures when using the dbinomLocal_normal function to describe y. 

Typically, if I had something like y[i] ~ dbinom(p_det, N_trials), I would set y[] <- NA and run the model without data to do a prior predictive check. Similarly, for discrepancy measures, I would do:

for(i in 1:M){ 
y.new[i] ~ dbinom(p_det, N_trials)
y.diff[i] <- y[i] - y.new[i]
} #end loop
pval_y <- mean(y.diff[1:M] > 0)

However, I can't seem to do either of these tasks using the dbinomLocal_normal. 

Do you have any suggestions for correct implementation? 

Here's a relevant section of my code: 

for(t in 18:30){
    for (i in 1:M){
     
      y[i, 1:5,t] ~ dbinomLocal_normal(detNums = detNums[i,t],
                                                     size = trials[1:n.traps,t],
                                                     p0 = p0,
                                                     detIndices = detIndices[i,,t],
                                                     s = s[i,1:2,t],
                                                     sigma = sigma,
                                                     trapCoords = trapCoords[1:n.traps,1:2],
                                                     localTrapsIndices = trapIndex[1:n.cells,1:maxNBDets],
                                                     localTrapsNum = nTraps[1:n.cells],
                                                     resizeFactor = resizeFactor,
                                                     habitatGrid = habitatIDDet[1:y.maxDet,1:x.maxDet],
                                                     indicator = z[i,t]*scrp[t],
                                                     lengthYCombined = lengthYCombined)
    }#i
  }#t

Thank you,
Heather Gaya

messages.subject: Re: NimbleSCR Prior Predictive Checks/Discrepancy
parts:
Hi Heather,

Thank you for your interest in the nimbleSCR package. I think it should be possible to implement both prior predictive checks and discrepancy measures as you described with the dbinomLocal_normal function.
What kind of problem/error message do you encounter when trying? 

One thing I can think of right now is that the dbinomLocal_normal (and other "local" functions in nimbleSCR) can take the detection history input in two different formats.
In the first one, "y" contains the number of detections of each individual at the different detectors it was detected, "detNums" contains the number of detectors at which this individual was detected, and "detIndices" contains the ID of the detectors at which the individual was detected.
In the second format, "y" contains all the above information collated in one single vector, i.e. c(detNums, y, detIndices), and the "detNums" and "detIndices" arguments are left empty. 

From the code you provided, it looks like you are using the first format. I think your problem when implementing prior predictive checks and discrepancy values is that this requires to call the random generation function (rbinomLocal_normal), which only works with the second input format.

What happens if you try to use the second format? 

You can also look at the vignette "Using nimbleSCR to simulate and fit Bayesian SCR models" where we simulate "y" from the model using the rbinomLocal_normal functionality.

Hope this helps,

Pierre Dupont.
